q-73610.name: Question 1
q-73610.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $M$ is given below. What are the pivot columns of $M?$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 9 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
q-73610.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $M$ has $3$ pivots in the $2$nd, $3$rd, and $5$th columns:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 9 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

q-73638.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]?
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & ↔{R}_{4} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

a
1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th only

1st, 3rd, and 5th only

d
1st, 3rd, 4th, and 5th only
e
1st, 2nd, and 3rd only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we need to convert P to row echelon form:

P=[204−100000400310000000−1−102]R2↔R5∼[204−100−1−102003100000000004]R4↔R5∼[204−100−1−102003100000400000]

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that P has 4 pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th columns.

q-35754.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}]?
$$
q-35754.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $2$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns.
